title: Por favor, ayúdame
goal: Give and follow instructions: commands for tú and usted, directions and recipes.

lessons.title: Tú commands
lessons.notes:
To tell a friend to do something, the **tú** command is easy: it's the same as the **él / ella** present form.
**habla** (speak) · **come** (eat) · **escribe** (write) · **cierra** (close - stem changes stay)
Eight common verbs have short forms worth memorising:
**ven** (come) · **ten** (have) · **pon** (put) · **sal** (go out) · **haz** (do, make) · **di** (say) · **ve** (go) · **sé** (be)
Add **por favor** to soften it, or turn it into a question: **¿Me ayudas?** is gentler than **ayúdame**.
In Spain, the plural for friends is **vosotros**: **hablad, comed** - in Latin America just use **ustedes** (next lesson).

sentences.en: Look! It's raining.
Listen to this song, it's really good.
accept_en: Listen to this song, it's great.

sentences.en: Wait a moment, please.
Close the window, it's cold.
Come here, I want to show you something.

accept_en: Set the glasses on the table.

sentences.en: Tell the truth.

lessons.title: Usted commands and directions
lessons.notes:
For **usted** (and **ustedes**), commands swap the vowel: **-ar** verbs take **-e**, **-er / -ir** verbs take **-a**. Start from the **yo** present and drop the -o:
**hablo -> hable** · **como -> coma** · **escribo -> escriba**
**tengo -> tenga** · **hago -> haga** · **vengo -> venga** · **pongo -> ponga**
For **ustedes**, add **-n**: **hablen, coman**.
Spelling keeps the sound: **doblar -> doble**, **cruzar -> cruce**, **seguir -> siga**.
You'll hear these from strangers giving directions:
**Siga todo recto, doble a la izquierda y cruce la calle.**

items.note: e -> i: sigo, sigue. Usted: siga.
Pase, por favor = Come in / After you.

sentences.es: Siga todo recto hasta el semáforo.
sentences.en: Keep going straight on to the traffic lights.
accept_en: Go straight on until the traffic lights.
Continue straight ahead to the lights.

sentences.es: Doble a la derecha en la esquina.

accept_en: Turn to the right at the corner.

sentences.es: Cruce la calle y el banco está a la izquierda.
sentences.en: Cross the street and the bank is on the left.
accept_en: Cross the road and the bank is on the left.

sentences.es: En el semáforo, doble a la izquierda.
sentences.en: At the traffic lights, turn left.
Take bus number twenty.
Come in, please. Have a seat.
accept_en: Come in, please. Take a seat.

sentences.en: Speak more slowly, please.
Be careful of the cars.

sentences.es: Coma menos sal y haga ejercicio.
sentences.en: Eat less salt and do some exercise.
accept_en: Eat less salt and do exercise.

lessons.title: Don't!
lessons.notes:
Negative **tú** commands use a different form: take the **usted** command and add **-s**:
**hable -> no hables** · **coma -> no comas** · **escriba -> no escribas**
**haga -> no hagas** · **venga -> no vengas** · **ponga -> no pongas** · **tenga -> no tengas**
Two you'll hear constantly: **no te preocupes** (don't worry) and **no vayas** (don't go, from ir).
For **usted**, just put **no** in front: **No hable.** · **No se preocupe.**
So the vowel swap (-ar -> e, -er / -ir -> a) is the key to all commands except positive tú.

sentences.es: No hables tan rápido, por favor.
sentences.en: Don't speak so fast, please.

sentences.es: No comas eso, está muy salado.

accept_en: Don't make any noise, the baby's asleep.
Don't make a noise, the baby is sleeping.

sentences.en: Don't go alone at night.
accept_en: Don't go on your own at night.

sentences.es: No te preocupes, todo está bien.
sentences.en: Don't worry, everything is fine.

sentences.en: Don't touch the oven, it's hot.

lessons.title: Help me! Commands with pronouns
lessons.notes:
With **positive** commands, pronouns are **attached to the end**, and an accent keeps the stress where it was:
**ayuda + me -> ayúdame** (help me) · **dime** (tell me) · **llámame** (call me)
Reflexive verbs too: **siéntate** (sit down) · **levántate** (get up) · **cálmate** (calm down)
Two pronouns, same order as before: **dámelo** (give it to me).
With **negative** commands, pronouns go **in front**, as usual:
**ayúdame** -> **no me ayudes** · **siéntate** -> **no te sientes** · **dímelo** -> **no me lo digas**
For **usted**: **ayúdeme**, **siéntese**, **dígame** (also how many people answer the phone).

items.note: e -> ie: me siento (same as I feel!).

sentences.en: Help me with the suitcases, please!
accept_en: Please help me with the suitcases!
Help me with the bags, please!

sentences.en: Tell me the truth.
Call me tomorrow morning.
Sit here, next to me.
accept_en: Sit down here, next to me.

sentences.en: Get up, it's already eight o'clock!

sentences.es: Es mi celular. Dámelo, por favor.
sentences.en: It's my phone. Give it to me, please.
accept_en: It's my mobile. Give it to me, please.

sentences.es: No me lo digas, ya lo sé.
sentences.en: Don't tell me, I already know.
accept_en: Don't tell me, I know already.

sentences.es: Cálmate, no es un problema grande.
sentences.en: Calm down, it's not a big problem.
accept_en: Calm down, it isn't a big problem.

sentences.es: Buenos días, señora. Siéntese, por favor.
sentences.en: Good morning, madam. Please sit down.
accept_en: Good morning, madam. Have a seat, please.
Good morning. Please take a seat.

sentences.es: No te sientes en esa silla, está rota.
sentences.en: Don't sit on that chair, it's broken.
accept_en: Don't sit in that chair, it's broken.
